items.title: Big Pharma, with eye on Anthropic, says AI is shrinking drug discovery timelines
items.summary: NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Artificial intelligence has sped up early-stage drug development work at some of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies this year, cutting by as much as half the time it takes to produce new molecules and move them into the clinic, according to their top scientists. GSK, Bristol Myers Squibb, Novartis, Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, AstraZeneca and Sanofi all say they have moved ‌beyond less glamorous tasks for AI like preparing regulatory filings.

items.title: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) Is Pushing Deeper Into Neuroscience
items.summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb (NYSE:BMY) reported first Phase 3 ADEPT clinical data for KarXT in psychosis linked to Alzheimer’s disease. The ADEPT program update highlighted initial findings on KarXT’s use in Alzheimer’s-related psychosis, addressing a significant treatment gap. Bristol Myers Squibb also entered a new clinical trial collaboration with Erasca to study MTAP-deleted pancreatic cancer using a molecular glue approach.
